findings.title: `sshQueueTransport` ignores the caller lifetime. A request can run past the caller deadline or abort.

findings.body:
**Pass the queue client and the remaining run budget to the deferred-context resolver.**

The default resolver call at `src/ops/review/address.ts:1001-1009` passes only the request object. The call therefore ignores `deps.queueClient`, so an injected client is bypassed on this path. The request also omits the remaining run budget. The loader then uses a 45-second per-invocation cap instead of the run budget, while the bookkeeping FIFO is held.

Wire the injected client through the default resolver:

<details>
<summary>Proposed wiring</summary>

```diff
-              const context = await (
-                deps.resolveDeferredVendorContext ?? resolveDeferredVendorContext
-              )({
+              const request = {
                 repoRoot: root,
                 target: input.target ?? 'merge-queue',
                 base: reviewedBase,
                 record,
                 onEvidenceImported: (evidence) => noteQueueEvidence(root, evidence),
                 ...(parent ? { signal: parent } : {}),
-              });
+              };
+              const context = deps.resolveDeferredVendorContext
+                ? await deps.resolveDeferredVendorContext(request)
+                : await resolveDeferredVendorContext(request, {
+                    ...(deps.queueClient ? { queueClient: deps.queueClient } : {}),
+                  });
```

Also add a `remainingMs?: () => number` field to `DeferredVendorContextRequest`. Set it from `remainingWallMs` at this call site. Forward it at `src/ops/review/internal/addressDeferred.ts:52` into the `options` object that `loadCurrentDeferredVendorDebt` receives.
</details>
findings.title: Pass the queue client and the remaining run budget to the deferred-context resolver.

findings.body:
**Register ledger bytes only for writes the default resolver requested.**

Lines 1010-1011 register the ledger file as engine-owned whenever the default resolver returns a context. `noteBookkeeping` hashes whatever bytes are on disk at that moment. It does not check that this call wrote them. This conflicts with the rule in `src/ops/review/run.ts`: "never bless bytes the engine did not request". `run.ts` registers only when the requested ledger equals the post-write ledger.

The unverified window is narrower than the original comment states. `loadCurrentWithLifetime` checks the ledger against its snapshot before the ancestry refresh. After that check, `refreshAuthorizedAncestry` performs queue reads. An external append in this window is not caught. Line 1011 then registers the foreign bytes, and the next bookkeeping check no longer detects them.

Two points limit a simple fix:
- The loader's own writes (`appendDebt` at lines 813 and 892) also need registration. An unconditional registration currently covers them. Removing line 1011 without a replacement would break those legitimate writes.
- The earlier claim that the loader writes and then returns `undefined` is incorrect. The loader returns `undefined` only before any write. A write followed by a thrown error leaves the write unregistered, because the resolver throws before line 1011.

Correction: register the ledger only when its current bytes match the content the default resolver's own mutations requested. Wrap the effects used by `resolveDeferredVendorContext` so that `mutate` records the requested ledger, as `run.ts` does. Pass the recorded value back to the caller for comparison.
findings.title: Register ledger bytes only for writes the default resolver requested.
